land.text: the County of Portugal, from the Minho to Coimbra (Cliopatria 1139-1146, 46,123 km2)

predecessors.note: The county-of-portugal dossier ends the county in 1143 (Zamora). The Kingdom page counts the kingdom from Ourique (25 July 1139 in the Afonso I and monarchs pages); Cliopatria's Kingdom row begins in 1147.

land.text: the metropole and the colonies, as the Republic's first Cliopatria shape (1911-1925, 2.2 M km2)

successors.note: Revolution of 5 October 1910. Cliopatria's own 1911 Kingdom shape (562 km2 at Praia) is an artifact. The colonies pass through the colony dossiers (portuguese-empire and portuguese-angola/mozambique).

capitals.name: Coimbra
capitals.note: Infobox 'Coimbra (until 1255)'; Sancho I 'was crowned in Coimbra' and Coimbra 'was the centre of his kingdom'.

capitals.name: Lisbon
capitals.note: Infobox 'Lisbon (1255-1910)'. António's government in exile sat at Angra do Heroísmo, Terceira, 1580-1582 (footnote) and Maria II's from 1830 to 1834.

capitals.name: Rio de Janeiro
capitals.note: 'From 1808 to 1821 Rio de Janeiro was the seat of the Portuguese court and the de facto seat of government' (footnote). The dot sits in Brazil, outside the metropole's land.

capitals.name: Lisbon
capitals.note: The court returns from Rio in 1821.

rulers.name: Afonso I (Afonso Henriques)
rulers.note: Reign counted from 25 July 1139 (Ourique); the kingdom's recognition at Zamora is 1143, this dossier's start. Clipped to 1143 by the eu-12-j reviewer so that the ruler span lies inside the dossier's life (reign from 1139).

rulers.name: Sancho II
rulers.note: List: reign ends 4 December 1247; his own page says he died 4 January 1248.

correction.text: the land of the former County of Portugal, from the Minho to the region of Coimbra, as a kingdom after Zamora: 'the Treaty of Zamora (1143) established peace between the cousins'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Cliopatria's Kingdom row begins in 1147 and labels 1139-1146 'County of Portugal' (46,123 km2, 39.58-42.11 N). The county-of-portugal dossier ends the county in 1143, so the kingdom takes that shape from 1143 to 1146. The Kingdom page gives Ourique as 25 July 1139 and Zamora as 5 October 1143 in the text (its infobox misprints 1139 for Zamora); Afonso I's page has him victorious at Ourique on 25 July 1139.

61,808 km2: the county plus the south bank reached in 1147, 'in 1147 he seized Santarém and Lisbon from the Moors'. Santarém 'was taken on 15 May 1147' in the page's footnote (the almoravid-dynasty dossier reads 15 March 1147 from another page). South edge 38.42 N is the Lisbon-Setúbal coast. The only infobox area is 90,000 km2 for 1300, so this shape is compared at 1250.
61,906 km2: the same 216 cells as 1147. Nothing on the page moves the border between 1147 and 1169; the 1179 bull Manifestis Probatum 'accepting the new king' changes no land.

70,237 km2: +32 cells in the Alentejo (38.4-39.57 N, 8.15-7.06 W). The page says Afonso 'also conquered an important part of the land south of the Tagus River' (later lost) and dates 1169 only to his capture by Ferdinand II of León; it names no Alentejo town and gives no year for the conquest. Year and extent are Cliopatria's: unverified: page budget.
68,008 km2: -9 cells (38.4-38.64 N), the southern Alentejo lost again. The page says only that the conquests south of the Tagus were later lost; 1177 is Cliopatria's: unverified: page budget.

61,690 km2: -23 cells (38.68-39.57 N), the Alentejo back to the 1152 line. The page has the Almohad caliph besiege Santarém in 1184 'defended by Afonso's son Sancho', and the shape keeps Santarém. Silves (1189-1191) is not in the shape; the ledger carries it.
61,787 km2: +1 cell (39.64 N, 7.22 W), below what any page opened can date; no event. The Kingdom page is silent on the 12th-century frontier: unverified: page budget.

61,809 km2: the same cell goes out again (-1); same cell set as 1188. No page opened dates it: unverified: page budget. Alcácer do Sal fell to Portugal in 1217 (ledger, Almohad Caliphate page); Cliopatria draws it only from 1220, a 10-cell lag left as is.

63,871 km2: +10 cells at 38.29-38.6 N, 8.79-8.06 W, the Sado estuary around Alcácer do Sal. The Almohad Caliphate page dates 'the loss of Alcácer do Sal to the Kingdom of Portugal in 1217' (ledger 1217); Cliopatria's step is three years late. Sancho II's page gives only 'From 1236 onwards'.

68,988 km2: +19 cells (38.79-39.57 N, 7.87-7.06 W: the Portalegre and Elvas country). No page opened dates them; the almohad-caliphate dossier reads the same step as a bridge: unverified: page budget.

correction.text: the 1236 shape without its two cells at Boulogne-sur-Mer (1.61-1.69 E, 50.62-50.75 N), which were never Portuguese land

keyframe_review.note: 69,672 km2: the shape adds two cells at Boulogne, in 1236-1240. Afonso (III) 'married Countess Matilda II of Boulogne in 1238', was Count of Boulogne 1238-1248 and 'abdicated his rights to the county of Boulogne in 1248'; he was the king's brother and count by marriage, not a king, and Boulogne was no part of the kingdom. The rest of the shape is the 1227 land (the Algarve and Alentejo conquests 'from 1236 onwards', Sancho II's page, are drawn from 1241).

86,396 km2: +60 cells (37.42-38.83 N, 8.76-7.06 W: the Baixo Alentejo and the eastern Algarve coast) and the Boulogne cells gone. The page says 'From 1236 onwards, Sancho II conquered several cities in the Algarve and Alentejo' but names none, so 1241 is Cliopatria's step in a conquest spread over 1236-1249.

91,911 km2: +18 cells (37.07-37.89 N), the Algarve complete: 'with the conquest of the Algarve in 1249' and Afonso is 'the first to use the title King of Portugal and the Algarve, from 1249'. Cliopatria draws it from 1250. Infobox 1300: 90,000 km2 against this shape's 91,911 km2 (ratio 1.02), within the tolerance. The shape runs to 1414 with no step at 1297: the Alcañices page says Denis 'gained Olivença' and the treaty 'defined the modern borders', a one-cell matter that the shape does not show.

region.text: the County of Portugal from the Minho to Coimbra, made a kingdom

ledger.note: 1143: the Treaty of Zamora makes Portugal a kingdom. The page's text has the second step 'on 5 October 1143' after Ourique ('26 July 1139' in the text, '25 July 1139' in the infobox, which also misprints Zamora as 5 October 1139); Afonso I's page says 'the Treaty of Zamora (1143) established peace between the cousins'. The dossier starts in 1143 so that it follows the county-of-portugal dossier, which ends the county then; the king is counted from 1139. The page names no boundary, so the core is the county's Cliopatria shape.

Same year, the page has him captured by Ferdinand II of León and obliged to surrender 'almost all the conquests' as his ransom; Cliopatria's shape shows no land north of the Minho.

region.text: the southern Alentejo of the 1169 shape

ledger.note: 1177: the southern part of the Alentejo conquest is gone (Cliopatria -9 cells, 38.4-38.64 N). The page says only that the conquests south of the Tagus were 'later lost'.

region.text: the northern Alentejo of the 1169 shape

ledger.note: 1188: the rest of the Alentejo conquest is gone (Cliopatria -23 cells, 38.68-39.57 N), the line of 1152 again; in 1184 'the Almohad caliph besieged Santarém, which was defended by Afonso's son Sancho'. The year is Cliopatria's; the page gives none.

region.text: the city of Silves and its district in the Algarve

ledger.note: 1189: Sancho I takes Silves. 'He used the title King of Silves from 1189 until he lost the territory to Almohad control in 1191.' The page does not say how or when in 1189; the almohad-caliphate dossier also has Portugal take the city in 1189. Not in Cliopatria's shape.

region.text: Silves, lost to the Almohads

ledger.note: 1191: Silves is lost again. 'Silves was again lost to the Moors in 1191.' The almohad-caliphate dossier dates the recapture to July 1191 from another page.

region.text: the Sado valley around Alcácer do Sal

ledger.note: 1217: Alcácer do Sal is taken from the Almohads. The Almohad Caliphate page: 'the loss of Alcácer do Sal to the Kingdom of Portugal in 1217 was an exception' (year only; the almohad-caliphate dossier has the same 1217 loss). The extent is Cliopatria's: it adds 10 cells around Alcácer do Sal (38.29-38.6 N, 8.79-8.06 W) only from 1220, so the drawn shape lags the event by three years. Year, source and confidence set by the eu-12-j reviewer (was 1220, confidence 1, Kingdom page silent).

region.text: the eastern Alentejo around Portalegre

ledger.note: 1227: Cliopatria adds 19 cells (38.79-39.57 N, 7.87-7.06 W: Portalegre and the Elvas country). No page opened dates it; the almohad-caliphate dossier bridges the same step with the same counterpart.

region.text: several cities in the Algarve and Alentejo, 1236 onwards

ledger.counterpart: Muslim rulers of the Algarve and Alentejo (not named on the page)
ledger.note: 1241: Cliopatria adds the Baixo Alentejo and the eastern Algarve coast (+60 cells, 37.42-38.83 N). The page says 'From 1236 onwards, Sancho II conquered several cities in the Algarve and Alentejo' and names none, so the year is Cliopatria's inside a conquest that runs 1236-1249.

region.text: the Algarve, conquered in 1249

ledger.counterpart: Muslim rulers of the Algarve and Alentejo (not named on the page)
ledger.note: 1249: the conquest of the Algarve is complete. 'with the conquest of the Algarve in 1249'; Afonso is 'the first to use the title King of Portugal and the Algarve, from 1249', the Algarve joining 'following the capture of Faro' (no date for Faro). Cliopatria draws it from 1250. Castile's Alfonso X returns the Algarve in 1263 according to the crown-of-castile dossier; the Afonso III page gives only 'a series of wars' and the 1267 treaty.
1255: the seat moves from Coimbra to Lisbon. Infobox: 'Coimbra (until 1255) Lisbon (1255-1910)'; Afonso III's page says he 'transferred the royal seat to Lisbon' without a year.

region.text: Olivença, which Denis 'gained'

ledger.note: 1297: the Treaty of Alcañices fixes the frontier with Castile and gives Portugal Olivenza. 'signed in Alcañices between King Denis of Portugal and King Fernando IV of Castile in 1297'; Denis 'gained Olivença' (the page does not say from whom: Castile as the other party is my reading); the treaty 'defined the modern borders between the two Iberian countries'. The page also says Denis went to war with Castile in 1295 'relinquishing the villages of Serpa and Moura', which can be read either way, so no Serpa or Moura event is entered. Cliopatria's shape shows no step in 1297.

1385: the House of Aviz succeeds the Burgundian dynasty. Infobox 'Avis dynasty: 15 October 1385'; the text ends the Afonsine line at 'the 1383-1385 Portuguese interregnum'. The List of Portuguese monarchs has John I reigning from 6 April 1385. The state, colour and land go on.

region.text: the Atlantic island of Madeira

ledger.note: 1419: the Portuguese reach Madeira. 'the Atlantic islands of Madeira (1419) and Azores (1427) were reached'; reached, not yet settled, and Cliopatria draws the islands from 1422. The portuguese-empire dossier also lists the islands as its gain (see notes).

region.text: the Atlantic islands of the Azores

ledger.note: 1427: the Portuguese reach the Azores. Same sentence of the Portuguese Empire page; Cliopatria draws the first cells in 1440 and the central islands in 1450.

region.text: Terceira, where António's government in exile sat

ledger.note: 1580: António holds the Azores. After the defeat he 'established a government in exile until 1583' (the Kingdom page's footnote has him and Mary II ruling from Angra do Heroísmo, 1580-1582 for António).

region.text: Santarém, where António was proclaimed, to Lisbon, where he was beaten

ledger.note: June 1580: the crown is contested. 'In June 1580, António proclaimed himself King of Portugal in Santarém'; the Habsburg armies of Philip II are the other claimant's. The page says whether Portugal 'was actually invaded by Spain is contested' and names no frontier crossing.

region.text: the land between Santarém and Lisbon

ledger.note: 25 August 1580: the mainland is lost to the claimant. 'His domestic government lasted until 25 August 1580, when he was defeated in the Battle of Alcântara.'

region.text: the kingdom of Portugal in personal union with Habsburg Spain, 1580 to 1640

ledger.note: April 1581: Philip II of Spain becomes Philip I of Portugal and the crowns are joined. He 'was acclaimed king in 1580 ... and recognized as official king by the Cortes of Tomar in 1581' (1580 crisis page); the List of Portuguese monarchs dates his reign from 17 April 1581, the infobox 'Philippine dynasty: 25 March 1581'. A personal union: 'the kingdom and its overseas territories should remain separate from Spain and keep their own laws and Cortes.' The land passes to the iberian-union dossier for 1582-1639 (Cliopatria's Iberian Union row), and this dossier has no keyframe for those years.

region.text: Terceira

ledger.note: 1583: the last Portuguese resistance ends. António's government on Terceira lasted 'until 1583'.

region.text: the kingdom, separate again from Spain

ledger.note: 1 December 1640: Portugal recovers its independence. 'On 1 December 1640, Antão Vaz de Almada, Miguel de Almeida and João Pinto Ribeiro assassinated Miguel de Vasconcelos', and John, Duke of Braganza, 'was acclaimed as John IV the same day'. The Kingdom page's infobox: 'Restoration of Independence: 1 December 1640'.
1640: the House of Braganza takes the throne. 'After the Portuguese Restoration War of 1640-1668, the kingdom passed to the House of Braganza'; John IV is acclaimed on 1 December 1640.

region.text: the Portuguese-Spanish frontier, Elvas and Badajoz to the Minho

ledger.note: May 1644: the first dated battle of the long frontier war. 'The Battle of Montijo near Badajoz, between the Portuguese and the Spanish, was fought on 26 May 1644'; Elvas withstood a nine-day siege that year. The war began on 1 December 1640 but the page dates no earlier engagement; the frontier is the whole raia from Monção (Minho, 1659) to Évora, Ameixial and Valencia de Alcántara (1663-1664).

region.text: the Portuguese-Spanish frontier

ledger.note: 13 February 1668: the Treaty of Lisbon ends the war. Spain recognised the Braganza dynasty; the pages opened name no change of Portuguese land in the terms. The summary table lists Ceuta and Hermisende as ceded to Spain; Ceuta is the empire's land, not in this dossier's shapes.

region.text: the Spanish interior from the frontier to Madrid that Cliopatria draws Portuguese in 1706-1708

ledger.note: May 1706: an Allied force from Portugal enters Madrid and Zaragoza. 'his absence allowed an Allied force from Portugal to enter Madrid and Zaragoza' (Portugal had 'joined the Grand Alliance in May 1703'). Portugal is the occupier here; the land stays Spanish (pro-habsburg-spain, Charles III's side, touches the shape in 1706-1708). Cliopatria draws a 60-cell corridor (7.42-3.94 W, 39.49-40.21 N) as Portuguese.

region.text: the Spanish interior

ledger.note: 1708: Cliopatria drops the corridor in 1709. The page dates only the Allied retreat of 1710 ('the Allies could not hold the interior and were forced to retreat') and is silent on the Portuguese frontier, so 1708 is a bridge.

region.text: Olivença and nearby Juromenha

ledger.note: 20 May 1801: Spain attacks Portugal. 'The Spanish attack on Portugal started on the early morning of 20 May'; 'Olivença and nearby Juromenha quickly surrendered to the Spanish forces'.

region.text: Olivença and nearby Juromenha

ledger.note: 9 June 1801: the War of the Oranges ends (infobox '20 May - 9 June 1801').

region.text: Olivença

ledger.note: 6 June 1801: the Treaty of Badajoz cedes Olivenza. 'On 6 June 1801 Portugal agreed to the tenets of the Treaty of Badajoz': to 'cede Olivenza to Spain' and close its ports to English ships. The Treaty of Madrid (29 September 1801) confirmed it; the infobox has 'Portuguese territory returned, except Olivenza, and border territories, which remained in Spanish possession', and Spain's Vienna signature asked the winning powers to 'return Olivença to Portuguese authority'. Juromenha is not on the loss list. The kingdom-of-spain dossier has the matching gain.

1808: the court is in Rio de Janeiro. 'From 1808 to 1821 Rio de Janeiro was the seat of the Portuguese court and the de facto seat of government' (footnote); the Portuguese Empire page: 'When the Portuguese court fled to Brazil in 1807'. The capital dot would leave the kingdom's land; the dossier records the page.

region.text: the Beiras and the Estremadura north of the Lines (Cliopatria's 65 cells, 9.26-6.91 W, 39.07-40.84 N)

ledger.note: August 1810: the French invade central Portugal. Almeida fell 'in August 1810', the Anglo-Portuguese Army fell back after winning the Battle of Buçaco 'on 27 September 1810' and 'Masséna's forces arrived at the lines on 11 October'. Portugal is the owner here (first-french-empire shapes cover the 65 cells in 1811, the occupier's row); the page does not say how much land the French held, so the zone is Cliopatria's 65 cells.

region.text: the Beiras and the Estremadura north of the Lines

ledger.note: April 1811: the French leave Portugal. 'Marshal Masséna ordered a retreat at the beginning of March 1811' and he 'returned to Spain in April 1811'.

1815: the kingdom becomes the United Kingdom of Portugal, Brazil and the Algarves, 'which existed between 1815 and 1822'. Brazil is not in this dossier's shapes (the portuguese-empire row carries it to 1823); only the name and title change.
1821: the court returns to Lisbon, the end of the 'seat of the Portuguese court' in Rio ('From 1808 to 1821'). The page gives no month.

7 September 1822: Brazil leaves. Pedro 'proclaimed the independence of Brazil on 7 September 1822'; the United Kingdom of 1815 ends and the Kingdom of Portugal (and the Algarves) goes on. Brazilian land is the portuguese-empire dossier's, so no loss is entered here.

region.text: the metropole, with Madeira and the Azores

ledger.note: 5 October 1910: the monarchy falls. Infobox 'Revolution of 1910: 5 October 1910'; the page ends in 'the collapse of the monarchy in the 5 October 1910 revolution'; Manuel II's reign ends that day (List of Portuguese monarchs). The land passes to the Portuguese Republic (Cliopatria 1911-1925).

wars.name: Portuguese Reconquista (Santarém and Lisbon to the Algarve)
belligerents: Muslim rulers of the Algarve and Alentejo

zones.text: the land south of the Tagus, won and lost until 1249

wars.outcome: Portugal takes Santarém and Lisbon (1147), holds the northern Alentejo 1169-1176, Silves 1189-1191, and completes the Algarve in 1249.
wars.note: A composite entry: the pages opened give 1147 (Afonso I), 1189-1191 (Sancho I), 'From 1236 onwards' (Sancho II) and 1249 (Afonso III). The Wikipedia article 'Reconquista' was not opened.

wars.name: Almohad offensive against Silves
wars.outcome: Sancho I is 'King of Silves from 1189 until he lost the territory to Almohad control in 1191'.

wars.name: Castilian-Portuguese wars over the Algarve
wars.outcome: The dispute 'led to a series of wars between the two kingdoms'; the Treaty of Badajoz (1267) fixed 'the southern border between Castile and Portugal' on the Guadiana. The Algarve stayed Portuguese.
wars.note: The page dates none of the wars (1250-1253 is not on it); the entry runs from the conquest to the treaty with no zone, because no campaign that took or held ground is dated.

wars.name: Castilian-Portuguese war of 1295-1297
wars.outcome: Ended by the Treaty of Alcañices (1297): Portugal 'gained Olivença', the Algarve was reaffirmed and the treaty 'defined the modern borders'.
wars.note: 'Denis went to war with Castile in 1295, relinquishing the villages of Serpa and Moura' is ambiguous on the page.

wars.name: War of the Portuguese Succession (1580 crisis)
wars.outcome: António is beaten at Alcântara on 25 August 1580; Philip II is recognised at Tomar in 1581; Terceira holds out 'until 1583'. A personal union with separate laws and Cortes.

wars.name: Portuguese Restoration War

zones.text: the frontier from Monção to Elvas, Badajoz and Valencia de Alcántara

wars.outcome: Portugal wins: Spain recognised the House of Braganza by the Treaty of Lisbon (13 February 1668); Portugal kept its other colonies but not Ceuta.
wars.note: Dated engagements: Montijo 26 May 1644, Monção 7 February 1659, Évora (Spanish, May 1663), Ameixial 8 June 1663, Valencia de Alcántara (Portuguese, July 1664), Montes Claros 17 June 1665. The page gives no Portuguese land change.

wars.name: War of the Spanish Succession (Portuguese front)

zones.text: the Spanish interior to Madrid, entered in 1706

wars.outcome: Portugal 'joined the Grand Alliance in May 1703'; an Allied force from Portugal entered Madrid and Zaragoza in 1706; the Allies were forced to retreat in 1710. The Peace of Utrecht is 11 April 1713 on the page, which has no Portuguese-Spanish terms.
wars.note: Cliopatria draws the 1706-1708 corridor as Portuguese; here it is an occupation (ledger).

wars.name: War of the Oranges
wars.outcome: Spain wins in 21 days (20 May - 9 June 1801); the Treaty of Badajoz (6 June) cedes Olivenza.

wars.name: French invasions of Portugal

zones.text: the Beiras and Estremadura north of the Lines, held by Masséna's army in 1810-1811

wars.outcome: Anglo-Portuguese victory: 'Marshal Masséna ordered a retreat at the beginning of March 1811' and returned to Spain in April 1811 (Lines of Torres Vedras page).
wars.note: The French-invasions page itself gives only 'campaigns between 1807 and 1810' and an infobox span of 1807-1811; Almeida (August 1810), Buçaco (27 September 1810) and the Lines (11 October 1810) are from the Lines page. Junot's 1807 and Soult's 1809 invasions are not dated on any page opened.

certainty.note: The Reconquista frontier (the Tagus line, the Alentejo and Algarve) is approximate; the Guadiana line of 1267 and the 1249 Algarve are the only fixed points.

The Treaty of Alcañices (1297) 'defined the modern borders between the two Iberian countries'; Olivenza is the exception after 1801; the 1706 Madrid corridor and the 1810-1811 French hold are occupations, not borders; the Atlantic islands are islands (no border to survey) and the colonies were never part of the kingdom's drawn land here.

notes:
ONE STATE, NOT TWO. Cliopatria's 'Kingdom of Portugal' runs 1147-1911 and the brief suspected successive states. It is one: the House of Burgundy, Aviz and Braganza follow without a break and the 1580-1640 union with Habsburg Spain was a personal union ('the kingdom and its overseas territories should remain separate from Spain and keep their own laws and Cortes'). Dynasty changes are rename events (1385, 1640). Cliopatria's 1581-1640 gap is the Iberian Union row (1582-1639): this dossier has a loss to iberian-union in 1581 and a gain in 1640 and no keyframes between.

START 1143, NOT 1139. The Kingdom page and Afonso I's page count the kingdom from Ourique (25 July 1139); the county-of-portugal dossier ends the county at the Treaty of Zamora (1143). I start at 1143 so that the two dossiers tile (Cliopatria itself labels 1139-1146 'County of Portugal'). The integrator may instead start the kingdom at 1139 and end the county then. The infobox of the Kingdom page misprints Zamora as 5 October 1139; the text says 1143. New keyframe kingdom-of-portugal_1143 (1143-1146) = the County of Portugal's Cliopatria shape.

OVERSEAS LAND REMOVED FROM THE METROPOLE. Cliopatria puts Ceuta, the Moroccan stations, Cape Verde, Mina, São Tomé, Muscat, the Persian Gulf (1521-1555 and 1564-1639, 257 cells) and, from 1824, patches of Angola and Mozambique (to 1.94 M km2 by 1895) into this row. The group scope asks for the metropole distinct from the overseas empire, and the colony dossiers exist (portuguese-empire, portuguese-morocco, portuguese-africa, portuguese-angola, portuguese-mozambique), so every shape from 1415 on is 'adjust': the Cliopatria cells inside modern Portugal. Consequences for the integrator: (1) Cliopatria's Muscat cells stay in the Kingdom row to 1705 although 'Muscat was captured by Oman under the Al-Ya'arubs in 1650' (Portuguese Empire page); the yarubid-dynasty ledger (1643, 1650) names kingdom-of-portugal as counterpart and should name portuguese-empire. (2) The intersect with modern Portugal also drops 7-8 edge cells (Olivenza, the Minho and Spanish-side border cells, about 2,000 km2) from 1415; the 1250 shape keeps them. (3) Madeira and Azores are kept in the metropole (today part of Portugal), but the portuguese-empire dossier also lists them as its gains (1419, 1427): they must be drawn once. Cliopatria's 1422/1440/1450 steps are settlement years, the page's 1419/1427 are 'reached'; Flores and Corvo (Azores) are not in the shape and the page is silent on them.

UNVERIFIED STEPS (page budget, 14 pages; four were thin: Sancho I, Sancho II, the French-invasions page and, for territory, the Kingdom page). 1169, 1177, 1188 (Alentejo gained and lost), 1202, 1216, 1220 (Alcácer do Sal), 1227 (Portalegre), 1241 (Baixo Alentejo, eastern Algarve), 1809, 1834 and 1836: the steps are Cliopatria's with confidence-1 bridge events, because no page opened gives the year and the land. The Almohad Caliphate page (cited by the almohad-caliphate dossier for Alcácer do Sal 1217) and the Reconquista, Conquest of Lisbon/Santarém, Treaty of Badajoz (1267) and Battle of Ourique pages were not opened; a gap-filler should read them. Santarém: this dossier's Afonso I page footnote says 15 May 1147, the almoravid-dynasty dossier has 15 March 1147 from another page.

DISAGREEMENTS. Treaty of Alcañices: the page says Denis 'gained Olivença' but not from whom, and 'relinquishing the villages of Serpa and Moura' can be read either way; no Serpa/Moura event. Sancho II's death: 4 January 1248 in the text and 4 November 1248 in his infobox (the monarch list ends his reign 4 December 1247). The infobox area is 90,000 km2 for 1300 against Cliopatria's 91,911 km2 (ratio 1.02); no other area is given.

COUNTERPARTS. almoravid-dynasty, almohad-caliphate, crown-of-castile, kingdom-of-spain and county-of-portugal have dossiers. iberian-union (eu-12), portuguese-republic and first-french-empire (eu-20) did not exist on 2026-10-31. 'Muslim rulers of the Algarve and Alentejo (not named on the page)' stands for the last Muslim holders of 1241-1249 (the taifa-of-niebla dossier is the likely neighbour, not checked). The pro-habsburg-spain dossier (Charles III's Spain, 1702-1708) is the ally of the 1706 advance; the occupation event names kingdom-of-spain, the owner of the land.

NOT RESEARCHED. The Liberal Wars of 1828-1834 (Miguel against Maria II, whose government sat on Terceira 1830-1834 per the Kingdom page's footnote) and the 1383-1385 interregnum are civil wars with no shape change; no page on them was opened, so no rebel dossier. Cliopatria shows no change for the Algarve 1263 return by Castile.

GAZETTEER NAMES. 'Olivenza' (place, Olivença, 38.68 N 7.10 W, Extremadura/Alentejo border) is used in four events and two wars and is not in places.jsonl. Boulogne-sur-Mer is given as a coordinate disk in the 1236 correction because the gazetteer lacks it.

REVIEW (eu-12-j, 2026-10-31): the Alcácer do Sal gain is dated 1217 from the Almohad Caliphate page (was a 1220 confidence-1 bridge); Afonso I's ruler span is clipped to 1143. The same page gives 'Beja in 1234 (to Portugal)', 'Silves in 1242 (to Portugal)' and the Almohad reconquest of southern Portugal in 1190-1191, leads for the 1177, 1188 and 1241 bridges.
